open_points.subject: scratch per-file setrlimit value
open_points.text: “the size of a file written in the scratch”
open_points.question: Which numeric bound is applied to the runner’s file-size setrlimit: `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, `output_bytes`, or another value?
options: Introduce a separate release or contract bound

open_points.subject: scratch-total accounting scope
open_points.text: “the apparent sizes of the distinct regular files (each inode once) under the exchange directory, the files the parent put there excluded”
open_points.question: Exactly which files are excluded or included when computing scratch total, especially parent-created inputs later modified or replaced, hard links to their inodes, and files created by the runner for protocol or returned outputs?
options: Exclude the original parent-provided inodes regardless of later links or modification; count every other regular-file inode
Exclude only the original parent-created paths while they still name the original files
Exclude all parent/runner protocol files and count only files directly created by agent code
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the original parent-provided inodes and count every other distinct regular-file inode, including runner-created output files.

open_points.subject: caught file-size limit
open_points.question: If the file-size setrlimit rejects a write but agent code catches the resulting signal or exception, deletes the file, and returns conforming output, must the execution still be `resource_exhausted`, and how is that hit made observable to the parent?
options: Any rejected write is a persistent limit hit and forces `resource_exhausted`
Only abnormal termination or final scratch accounting establishes a hit
A caught file-size error may be handled by the function and does not itself force failure
open_points.default_guess: Any rejected write remains recorded by the runner and forces `resource_exhausted`.

open_points.subject: scratch measurement and cleanup ordering
open_points.text: “The scratch total is measured once, when the environment has ended” and “An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed”
open_points.question: At what exact point is scratch measured relative to output collection, process reaping, exchange-directory removal and confirmation of cleanup, and which outcome wins if scratch is excessive but cleanup also cannot be confirmed?
options: Measure after all processes are reaped and outputs collected but before removal; the stated outcome order makes `resource_exhausted` win
Measure before process reaping and removal; later cleanup failure overrides it with `crashed`/`cleanup_failed`
Measure after cleanup confirmation using accounting retained by the parent
open_points.default_guess: Measure after reaping and output collection but before removal, and apply the stated outcome order so `resource_exhausted` wins.

open_points.subject: execute_function resources_used
open_points.question: Now that the sandbox measures a final scratch total and enforces a per-file scratch limit, must `execute_function` include either measurement in `resources_used`, and if so which values and on which outcomes?
options: Report final scratch total and maximum regular-file size for every outcome where measurement completed
open_points.default_guess: Report the final scratch total whenever measurement completed, but not the configured per-file limit.
